Subject: Procurement questionnaire: details on measurements, alerts, and metric access

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for engaging with Stellar Data on this deal. Procurement sent over a short SLA questionnaire and asked for specific evidence about how Redwood measures and exposes availability and latency SLOs. Please find the attached form (procurement-sla-form.xlsx). High-level ask: we need a short, audit-ready response that covers how availability/latency are calculated, alert thresholds, retention, and what read-only or export access we can provide to customers.

Key items they flagged:
- Definition of availability and measurement interval (how you handle rolling windows / partial availability)
- P95/P99 latency measurement methodology and sample windows
- Alerting triggers and Escalation paths (who sees them, SLAs for incident response)
- Customer-facing dashboards vs. raw telemetry export options
- Evidence: screenshots or exportable reports for the last 90 days

Can you send a succinct response and any supporting artifacts? Procurement would like the reply by EOD Friday (Nov 6) so they can include it in the contract binder. If there's anything we cannot share, please call that out and propose an exception path.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if useful.

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: details on measurements, alerts, and metric access

Hi Sarah,

Appreciate the clear list — below is a concise response you can drop into your binder. I attached a one-page evidence summary (redwood-sla-evidence-summary.pdf) and a Grafana invite template (grafana-invite-template.txt) that we use when provisioning read-only dashboards. If you need anything more formal (SOC2 artifacts, raw logs), flag it and we’ll follow the exception path.

Summary answers (for procurement binder):

1) Availability definition and measurement
- SLA metric: "API availability" = percent of successful inference requests (2xx) over the total accepted requests, per region and per model variant.
- Measurement window: rolling 30-day and 90-day windows; primary contractual measurement is 30-day rolling for monthly settlement, 90-day rolling for trend analysis.
- Partial outages: availability is computed as weighted by request volume per backend; short-lived pod restarts are included in the numerator/denominator (we do not drop requests unless explicitly syntax/validation failures).

2) Latency methodology (P95/P99)
- Latency measured at ingress point (time to first byte and time to final token) with request sampling across all frontends.
- P95 and P99 computed on successful requests over the same 30-day and 90-day windows. Sampling: full aggregation for production traffic; for extremely high-volume customers we use reservoir sampling to compute percentiles while preserving performance.

3) Alerting and incident handling
- Alert tiers:
  • Warning: single-window P95/P99 deviation > 1.5x baseline for 10m -> paging to on-call (Ops).
  • Incident: sustained error-rate > 1% or availability drop > 5% across a 5m window -> immediate paging + incident bridge.
- Escalation: on-call -> SRE lead -> Head of Infra. SLA credits require incident postmortem within 7 business days.

4) Customer access to metrics and evidence
- Read-only dashboard: we provision a Grafana read-only invite (URL provided) that shows availability, latency distributions, request counts, and per-model traces.
- Raw telemetry export: standard offer includes 90-day metrics exports (CSV) for Dedicated and Hosted Enterprise customers. Extended retention/export (60-365 days) can be provided for Dedicated or Private deployments via add-on.
- Audit window: default audit package includes daily PDFs for the last 90 days; temporary elevated access (S3 export of logs or a one-time raw export) can be granted for 30–60 days under an audit clause.

5) Evidence items attached
- redwood-sla-evidence-summary.pdf (one-page with Grafana screenshots and sampling definition)
- grafana-invite-template.txt (example invite text and scope)

Exceptions and commercial notes:
- We generally do not provide full raw request payloads for privacy/legal reasons; we can provide redacted logs or aggregated telemetry.
- Extended retention and long-term raw export are add-ons; Sales can propose pricing for a 60- or 180-day export window.

Next steps:
- If Stellar wants a 60-day temporary audit window or 180-day retention, tell me and I’ll loop Sales/Legal to propose pricing/terms.
- If you want the Grafana read-only link now, I can provision it and add your procurement contact.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0162
